name: Yemisi Strand-Kowalczyk
description:
Yemisi Strand-Kowalczyk is a solo neural-feed composer operating out of a converted water treatment node in the Circuit's eastern ward, active since 2211. Her work layers Yoruba talking-drum rhythms against glacially slow Nordic drone progressions, all threaded through a custom BCI rig that translates her REM-state neural activity into melodic data in real time. The result is something listeners describe as 'being held still by something enormous' — slow, tidal, emotionally precise music that arrives not through speakers but directly into the auditory cortex with haptic undertones that simulate the feeling of cold water rising.

Strand-Kowalczyk releases exclusively through pirate neural feed under the handle STRAND/SIGNAL, refusing all Vantablack overtures despite significant pressure. Her 2218 long-form piece 'Sediment' — a 74-minute composition designed to be experienced during sleep — became a Circuit phenomenon after dock workers started trading the feed chip as a sleep aid. She has never performed live, communicating only through encrypted text drops on mesh boards. Her identity as a Circuit resident was confirmed only when Vantablack security attempted a feed-block that she publicly routed around in real time.
creator: Yemisi Strand-Kowalczyk
audience: Circuit shift workers, insomniacs, augmentation recovery patients, mid-tier tech laborers seeking decompression
cultural_impact: Strand-Kowalczyk's refusal to corporatize has made her a Circuit folk hero and a recurring symbol in labor solidarity rhetoric. Her music is frequently cited by occupational wellness advocates as genuinely therapeutic for augmentation fatigue, a condition Vantablack-aligned healthcare labels refuse to formally recognize. The corporate blackout on her work has paradoxically made her the most-shared pirate feed in the Circuit for three consecutive years.
story_hooks: A Vantablack subsidiary has quietly placed a bounty on identifying Strand-Kowalczyk's physical location — not to prosecute her, but to acquire her BCI rig schematics, which appear to contain undocumented neural-interface architecture.

A character wakes from augmentation surgery to find 'Sediment' playing on their ward's unauthorized feed chip — and realizes the music contains a hidden data packet embedded in the subfrequency layer.
Strand-Kowalczyk breaks her silence and sends a single encrypted message to a journalist: a set of coordinates and the words 'before they close it.'
